sentences.text: Muscarinic acetylcholine receptors , or mAChRs , are acetylcholine receptors that form G protein-receptor complexes in the cell membranes of certain neurons and other cells .	G protein-receptor complexes	G protein-coupled receptor	neurons	neurons	cell	Cell (biology)	acetylcholine	acetylcholine

They play several roles , including acting as the main end-receptor stimulated by acetylcholine released from postganglionic fibers in the parasympathetic nervous system .	acetylcholine	acetylcholine	postganglionic fibers	postganglionic fibers	parasympathetic nervous system	parasympathetic nervous system
Muscarinic receptors were named as such because they are more sensitive to muscarine than to nicotine .	muscarine	muscarine	nicotine	nicotine

Their counterparts are nicotinic acetylcholine receptors -LRB- nAChRs -RRB- , receptor ion channels that are also important in the autonomic nervous system .	acetylcholine	acetylcholine	autonomic nervous system	autonomic nervous system

Many drugs and other substances -LRB- for example pilocarpine and scopolamine -RRB- manipulate these two distinct receptors by acting as selective agonists or antagonists .	pilocarpine	pilocarpine	scopolamine	Hyoscine hydrobromide
